issues.t: Cracked plastic intake manifold coolant passage (4.6L)
issues.sym: Coolant leaking at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, a dropping coolant level, and possible overheating.
issues.why: The early composite intake manifold has a plastic coolant crossover that can crack with age. Ford later revised the design.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Have the manifold inspected and replaced with an updated version.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger only shows up if the airbag deploys.
issues.why: These cars used Takata inflators that can degrade over time and rupture during a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls and get the free repair done as soon as possible.

issues.t: Water leaking onto the front floor
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the front footwell, a musty smell, and sometimes electrical glitches.
issues.why: Water can enter through body seals around the cowl or doors. Moisture near the wiring and junction box can cause corrosion.
issues.next: Have the leak path found and sealed, then dry the carpet fully. Check connectors in the footwell for corrosion.

issues.t: Coolant loss into the cylinders (2.3L EcoBoost)
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no visible leak, white exhaust smoke, misfires, or a rough start.
issues.why: Owners and a class action describe coolant seeping into the cylinders, which points to a head gasket or block sealing problem on these engines.
issues.next: Do not keep topping off without a diagnosis. Have a cooling system pressure test and a cylinder leak check done soon to avoid engine damage.

issues.t: Hard shifting and grinding (MT82 manual)
issues.sym: Gears grind or are hard to select, especially when cold or during quick shifts.
issues.why: The MT82 six-speed manual has a long record of shift quality complaints and synchronizer wear, and Ford issued bulletins about it.
issues.next: Have the clutch and shift linkage checked and the fluid changed to the correct type. Ask a dealer about any applicable bulletins.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic shifts (10-speed automatic)
issues.sym: Abrupt, clunky, or delayed shifts, especially at low speeds.
issues.why: The 10-speed automatic relies on adaptive software. Many complaints were addressed with software updates, and the issue led to legal claims.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for software updates and run a transmission relearn.

issues.t: Oil cooler hose separation (GT350 recall)
issues.sym: Sudden oil loss, smoke, or a low oil pressure warning.
issues.why: An oil cooler hose could come loose from its fitting. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If oil pressure drops, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic may not hold in Park (2018 recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the car can still creep or roll, especially on a slope. There may be no warning message.
issues.why: A small pin inside the 10-speed automatic may have been left out at the factory, so the transmission can lose its Park function over time. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until this is done. Check your VIN for the recall and have the free inspection and repair carried out right away.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic may not engage Park (2022-2023 recall)
issues.sym: The car may roll after you select Park, or the transmission may not lock when parked.
issues.why: A bolt inside the 10-speed automatic may be loose and can keep the park gear from engaging. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN for the recall and book the free repair right away.

issues.t: Rear suspension knuckle may have a casting flaw (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the part fails, the rear of the car can suddenly feel loose or unstable.
issues.why: Some rear knuckles, the part that carries the rear wheel, were cast with a flaw and can break. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the free inspection done before driving the car hard. Stop driving if the rear end feels unstable.

issues.t: Clutch line can melt against the exhaust on manual cars (recall)
issues.sym: A clutch pedal that goes soft or stays down, trouble shifting, a brake fluid warning, or fluid and smoke under the car.
issues.why: On manual-transmission cars the clutch pressure line can touch hot exhaust parts and melt. The clutch shares its fluid with the brakes, so a leak can affect both and the fluid can catch fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get the free repair right away. Stop driving if the clutch pedal changes feel or you smell burning.

issues.t: Engine bay wiring ground can break (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power, or the headlights, washers, A/C or cooling fan quitting.
issues.why: Ground connections in the engine bay wiring harness can fracture, cutting power to whatever they feed. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the free repair done right away. Pull over safely if the car loses power or the headlights go out.

issues.t: Cruise control cable can hold the throttle open (recall)
issues.sym: The engine keeps pulling after you lift off the gas, or the idle stays high.
issues.why: The cruise control cable can bind against the throttle linkage so the throttle does not return all the way to idle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done free. Until then, use the brake and shift to neutral if the engine will not slow down.

issues.t: Parking brake can let go on manual cars (recall)
issues.sym: The lever feels like it sets, then the car creeps or rolls away on a slope.
issues.why: The self-adjusting pawl in the parking brake can skip over its teeth so the brake does not hold.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Until it is fixed, leave the car in gear and turn the wheels into the curb when you park on a hill.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractor pin may be faulty (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can feel. The belt may lock or retract oddly.
issues.why: A malformed pin in the front seat belt retractor can keep the belt from holding the way it should in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the retractor replaced free.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can catch on the carpet (Cobra recall)
issues.sym: The pedal sticks or does not come back up when you lift your foot.
issues.why: On these supercharged Cobras the accelerator pedal can snag on the floor carpet.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the pedal sticks while driving, brake firmly, shift to neutral and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Timing chain guides wear out on the 4.0L V6
issues.sym: A rattle or death-rattle from the back of the engine on startup that may quiet down as it warms up.
issues.why: The plastic chain guides and the tensioners behind the timing cover wear and break up, so the chains slap and can jump.
issues.next: Have it looked at promptly. A jumped chain on this engine bends valves, and the job gets much bigger once that happens.

issues.t: Plastic thermostat housing cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Sweet-smelling coolant dripping at the front of the engine, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The housing is plastic and goes brittle with heat cycles until it splits at the seam or around the outlet.
issues.next: Get it replaced before it lets go completely, and do not keep driving an engine that is losing coolant.

issues.t: Rear axle pinion seal seeps gear oil
issues.sym: A damp film or drips on the front of the rear axle housing, sometimes a whine from the back of the car.
issues.why: The seal where the driveshaft meets the axle hardens with age and lets gear oil out, and road grit in.
issues.next: Have the seal replaced and the axle refilled. Running the axle low on oil ruins the gears and bearings.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioner cable can corrode and break (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see day to day. The belt may feel normal right up to a crash.
issues.why: The steel cable in the front belt pretensioner can corrode and snap, so the belt does not tighten in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get the free repair done.

issues.t: Backup camera picture is distorted or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The reversing picture is blank, upside down, snowy or comes and goes.
issues.why: Loose or damaged camera wiring, and on later cars a camera fault, stops the image reaching the screen.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls. Until it works, turn and look behind you before reversing.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can come up blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital cluster stays dark at startup, so you have no speedometer or warning lights.
issues.why: A fault in the cluster software or display leaves the screen blank when the car is switched on.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls. Do not drive far with no speedometer or warning lights.

issues.t: Reverse lights, camera and driver aids can switch off on manual cars (recall)
issues.sym: No reversing picture, no reverse lights, and features like blind spot or cross-traffic alerts stop working.
issues.why: The powertrain control software on these manual-gearbox cars may not tell the rest of the car that reverse is selected.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Reverse with your own eyes and mirrors until it is reprogrammed.

issues.t: Low brake fluid warning may never appear (recall)
issues.sym: No warning message even when the brake fluid is low, and the pedal slowly feels longer.
issues.why: The body control software may not turn the low brake fluid warning on.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls and check the fluid level yourself in the meantime.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a long crank, or the engine cutting out and not restarting.
issues.why: The pump inside the tank can fail and stop feeding fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get it done. A stall in traffic is a real risk.

issues.t: Steering can turn on its own from a sensor calibration fault (recall)
issues.sym: The wheel pulls or nudges to one side by itself, or the steering feels uneven.
issues.why: The steering torque sensor can be calibrated wrongly, so the power assist applies steering you did not ask for.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls and get it corrected before driving at speed.

issues.t: Water can knock out the tail and marker lights (recall)
issues.sym: Tail lights, plate light or side marker lights stop working, often after rain or a wash.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear lighting circuit and disable those lights, so traffic behind cannot see you.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Avoid driving in the dark until the lights work again.

issues.t: Headlight driver modules can fail (recall)
issues.sym: One or both headlights go out, flicker, or only part of the beam lights up.
issues.why: The LED driver module that powers the headlight can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and avoid night driving until both headlights work.

issues.t: Wipers may only run on high and washers may not work in the cold (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers jump straight to fast speed with no intermittent or slow setting, and the washers do nothing in freezing weather.
issues.why: A wiper and washer control fault leaves the system stuck on one speed and can stop washer flow in the cold.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Keep the glass clean and avoid driving in heavy rain or snow until it is fixed.

issues.t: Piston faults can damage the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking or rattling under load, a loss of power, or the engine shutting down.
issues.why: Some engines were built with defective piston domes or with piston circlips that were not seated properly, which can let the piston come apart.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls right away and stop driving if the engine knocks or loses power.

issues.t: EGR valve can fail and cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: A check engine light with rough running or a sudden drop in power.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve can fail and upset how the engine runs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done before a long trip.

issues.t: Spark plug can blow out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A loud pop or bang from the engine, then a constant chuffing or exhaust-like blowing noise, a heavy misfire, loss of power and a check-engine light.
issues.why: The aluminium heads hold each spark plug with only a few threads. Heat cycles and over-tightening strip those threads, and cylinder pressure then pushes the plug straight out.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it inspected. A steel thread insert normally saves the head, but carrying on can ruin the threads completely and burn the coil, boot and nearby wiring.

issues.t: Fuel pump driver module fails and the car stalls
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or cranks and cranks without starting. It often runs again after sitting a while, then quits at random, and a fuel pump code may be stored.
issues.why: The module that controls the fuel pump is bolted to the frame rail behind a rear wheel, where road spray and salt corrode its case and connector until it stops driving the pump.
issues.next: Have the module and its plug checked before the next long trip. Losing fuel pressure in moving traffic is the real hazard, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Paint peeling off the hood
issues.sym: The clear coat and color on the hood go cloudy, then flake or peel away in patches, usually after a few years outdoors. Some owners also see it on the hood scoop or the top of the front bumper.
issues.why: The top layers of factory paint lose their grip on the panel underneath, and sun exposure speeds it up on flat, horizontal surfaces like the hood. Owners report Ford would not cover it once the car was out of warranty.
issues.next: This is cosmetic, not a safety problem. Wash and wax the area to slow the spread, and get a body shop quote to strip and repaint the hood when you are ready, since spot touch-ups rarely hold on peeling clear coat.
